record.paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
record.original_question: Let X1 and X2 be cubic fourfolds. If there is an equivalence Ku(X1) ~= Ku(X2) between their Kuznetsov components, must X1 and X2 be birational?

evidence.quote: Does a Birational Categorical Torelli theorem

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^5$ be a smooth cubic fourfold over $\mathbb{C}$. The Kuznetsov component of $X$ is the full triangulated subcategory
$$\mathrm{Ku}(X) := \{ E \in D^b(X) : \mathrm{Hom}^\bullet(\mathcal{O}_X(i), E) = 0 \text{ for } i = 0, 1, 2 \} \subset D^b(X),$$
so that there is a semiorthogonal decomposition $D^b(X) = \langle \mathrm{Ku}(X), \mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{O}_X(1), \mathcal{O}_X(2) \rangle$. The subcategory $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ is a 2-Calabi–Yau category with the same Hochschild homology as a K3 surface.

Question: Let $X_1, X_2$ be two smooth complex cubic fourfolds. Assume there exists a $\mathbb{C}$-linear exact equivalence of triangulated categories
$$\mathrm{Ku}(X_1) \simeq \mathrm{Ku}(X_2).$$
Must $X_1$ and $X_2$ be birational?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether equivalence of Kuznetsov components of two cubic fourfolds implies birationality is posed as an open problem in recent surveys on categorical Torelli theorems. Known results give a categorical Torelli theorem up to compatibility with the degree-shift/rotation functor, but the unconditional birational version remains open. Analogous birational categorical Torelli statements have been proved in some Gushel–Mukai cases, but not for general cubic fourfolds.

status_evidence.snippet: Question 7.8 asks whether a Birational Categorical Torelli theorem holds for cubic fourfolds.
status_evidence.claim: The birational categorical Torelli question for cubic fourfolds is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Derived categories of cubic fourfolds (Kuznetsov)
status_evidence.snippet: The Kuznetsov component Ku(X) is a 2-Calabi–Yau category that behaves like the derived category of a K3 surface.
status_evidence.claim: Background on Ku(X) for cubic fourfolds; no birational Torelli is established here.
